newsitem.title: UK: Oldest British cars mark freedom of road centenary.
newsitem.headline: Oldest British cars mark freedom of road centenary.

text.p: British enthusiasts wheeled out some of the world's oldest cars on Sunday to celebrate 100 years of freedom of the road.
The 1896 Highways Act repealed a law which required a man carrying a red flag to walk in front of motor vehicles. It also raised the speed limit to 14 miles (22 km) an hour from four (six km).
The centenary led to a bumper turn-out for the annual London-to-Brighton rally in which vintage cars drive the 56 miles (90 km) from the capital to England's south coast.
Some 622 vehicles, almost 140 more than last year, left Hyde Park on the journey, although some broke down along the route.

Prince Michael of Kent, a cousin of Queen Elizabeth, took part in a 1903 De Dietrich, but was beaten to the finishing line by two even older cars -- a Panhard Levassor and a Stephens both dating from 1898.
